inputs.text: They’re presenting Abinader’s France agenda as a transparency push, but the real story is who gets to define “integrity” for the Dominican Republic. On 25 March 2026 in Paris, Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed an agreement to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, with Abinader there to witness it. That sounds less like proof of clean government than a carefully staged move to wrap policy in international approval—and make outside standards look like neutral oversight.
